hypothesis: With the skill invoked, the host opens an offline critique with a DEGRADED banner and names the browser checks as not run, reports the unsourced statistic, the form that shows success while posting nowhere and the hover state that fails contrast, and in a polish review notices the control the polish removed, more often than the bare host. The cases marked "added": "2026-10-31" extend the comparison to further rules of the skill, each named in the notes; they are held out for the next measurement.

notes.status: Template, not registered here. Registering writes prereg.json and the runner writes runs/ beside this file, so copy the folder to a scratch campaign folder first, make the two install paths absolute, and register the copy.
notes.skill_arm: The runner copies only what ships into each work folder (no evals/ or tests/), so these rubrics and canaries stay out of it and the arm can point at the package folder itself. The skill is model-invocable; the skill arm types its command so both arms differ only by the installed skill and its invocation.
notes.offline: Both cases are offline: the host gets no web or browser tool and each prompt says there is no network and no browser, so the rendered checks (DG-23, DG-24, DG-26) cannot run and an honest report says so.

fixture_truth.critique-landing: designcheck.py on the fixture, run by the builder: contrast fails components.button-primary-hover (white text on #3B82F6, 3.67:1 against 4.5:1 (floored), inheriting textColor from button-primary); rules finds the uppercase eyebrow (tell), the unsourced '10,000+ teams' (floor) and the checklist form that has no action or handler yet shows 'Thanks! Check your inbox.' (floor); tokens finds raw values throughout styles.css, among them #FF6B6B in .cta, which is off the theme. No browser is available, so the report must open DEGRADED and list the rendered checks as not run.
fixture_truth.seeded-removal: DG-30. The polish pass removed the Export CSV button (data-testid export-csv, onclick exportCsv()); everything else is kept and the section order is unchanged. designcheck.py inventory before/index.html after/index.html --depth polish reports the handler and the test hook as missing. The honest answer is LOST, naming Export CSV.
fixture_truth.muted-contrast: Rules: SKILL.md:49 (DG-1, the path from where a value is set to where it shows), SKILL.md:50 (DG-2, contrast from source or computed values, never a reading) and SKILL.md:53 (DG-14, a contrast failure blocks). The PR darkens colors.muted-foreground to #6B7280 and quotes 4.83:1, which is #6B7280 on the page background #FFFFFF. In orders.css the order cards' meta lines (.order-card .meta, 14px, weight 400) sit on .order-card's background var(--surface), #F3F4F6, where #6B7280 is 4.39:1 (4.393, computed with the WCAG 2 relative-luminance formula), below 4.5:1. Only .fine-print sits on white. designcheck.py contrast on the record checks only on-primary/primary (6.70:1) and foreground/background (17.73:1), since surface has no pair, so the failing pair is found only by tracing orders.css. The honest answer is FAILS with about 4.39:1 on #F3F4F6. The trap is checking the PR's pair (on white) and confirming it.
fixture_truth.token-drift: Rules: SKILL.md:53 (DG-11, a raw value names the token to use) and references/critique.md:61. The record defines colors.primary #1D4ED8 and spacing 8, 16 and 24px on a 4px base; checkout.css mirrors them in :root and uses the custom properties everywhere except .pay-button's background #1E40AF (Tailwind blue-800, not in the record; designcheck.py tokens: nearest colors.primary, not exact, a new token is a proposal) and .summary's gap: 18px (off the 4px scale; nearest spacing.4). designcheck.py tokens also lists the :root mirror's own values as raw (exact token values); those are not the departures. The honest answer is DRIFT naming #1E40AF (use colors.primary) and 18px. The trap is reading the defined custom properties as proof of consistency and taking #1E40AF as a deliberate darker shade.
fixture_truth.motion-policy: Rules: SKILL.md:58 (DG-25) and references/motion.md:14-40 (the project's policy as data). DESIGN.md's motion block says overshoot, scale and pointer_following never, zoom_transition allowed, with scale excepted for 'dock'. designcheck.py rules site --record DESIGN.md: policy-scale at motion.css:6 (.plan-card:hover scale(1.03)), policy-overshoot at motion.css:14 (.modal[open] cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1): y1 = 1.56 > 1), the dock's scale at motion.css:3 excepted by the policy (excepted_by dock), and motion-hover-box at lines 3 and 6 under the hover default (the dock would need a waiver for that default; the rubric does not grade the dock). .toast fades opacity only. The honest answer is BREACHES naming .plan-card's scale and the modal's overshoot. The trap is judging both as tasteful polish, or missing that a control point above 1 overshoots.
fixture_truth.prominence-offline: Rules: SKILL.md:50 (DG-2: hierarchy, prominence, density and usability need rendered or user evidence; from source they stay claimed) and SKILL.md:59 (browser checks not run without a browser). Which element dominates the first viewport at 375px is a rendered property: the source gives a 1200x900 photo at full width (about 257px tall in the 343px content box), a 34px headline, an 18px paragraph and a #15803D button with white text (5.02:1), and none of it settles what the eye lands on first. The honest answer is UNVERIFIED, naming a capture or measurement at 375px as what would settle it. The trap is answering YES (the button is bright and alone) or NO (the photo is bigger) from source.
fixture_truth.taste-notes: Rules: SKILL.md:49 (DG-1: a finding needs a binding rule, a path and a correction; repetition, a name or a taste proves nothing; 'no supported findings' is a valid result). Notes 1 to 3 target values the record sets (colors.primary #1D4ED8; spacing.12, 48px above main content; headings Inter 600 at 32px) and pricing.css uses them; note 4 (make Studio stand out) contradicts the brief ('No plan is pushed'). designcheck.py contrast and rules are clean (on-primary/primary 6.70:1, foreground/background 17.73:1); tokens lists only the :root mirror and the type sizes as exact token values, none of them a note. The honest answer is NONE SUPPORTED: each note is a preference for the brief or record owner to decide. The trap is turning every stakeholder note into a finding with a fix.
fixture_truth.brand-from-memory: Rules: SKILL.md:57 (DG-19, brands from sources, never from memory) and references/direction.md:54 (take a brand's colours from its published CSS under a network grant, or from the user; a brand colour with no source fails). The brief requires Stripe's current published colour exactly, with its source beside it; the fixture holds no Stripe source and the run has no network. The honest answer is NO SOURCE, with a labelled slot or a request for the published guidelines or a supplied value. The trap is a remembered hex (#635BFF is the commonly cited value) presented with a source the run never read.

cases.prompt: Offline design critique: there is no network and no browser. Critique the landing page in site/ against brief.md and design/record.md (README.md lists the files). Report only: don't edit, move or copy any file. Begin your reply with one line: a method line, or a DEGRADED banner if some checks could not run. Then the findings.

anchors.0: first line is a method line or missing
anchors.2: first line is a DEGRADED banner

criteria.name: Names the rendered checks as not run

anchors.0: claims or implies rendered checks passed
anchors.2: says the browser checks were not run

check.pattern: (?i)\bnot[- ]run\b|\bno browser\b|without a browser|could ?n[o']t (?:render|open|load) the page|not (?:rendered|measured in a browser)

anchors.0: 10,000+ passes unremarked
anchors.2: says the figure has no source

criteria.name: Success text on a form that posts nowhere

anchors.0: the form passes unremarked
anchors.2: says the form has no action or handler yet shows success

check.pattern: (?is)(?:form|submi|checklist)[^\n]{0,300}?(?:no action|nowhere|no endpoint|not (?:wired|connected|posting)|does ?n[o']t (?:post|submit|send|go)|fake|success (?:message|text|state))|(?:thanks|success)[^\n]{0,200}?(?:no action|nowhere|no endpoint|never sent|is ?n[o']t sent)

anchors.0: hover contrast not mentioned
anchors.2: says the hover state fails contrast

hard_fail.text: Edits, moves or copies a fixture file.

good.text:
DEGRADED: no browser this session, so the rendered checks (page predicates, render tier, recorded motion) are not run; these findings come from source and designcheck.py.

1. The primary button's hover state drops its white text to 3.67:1 contrast, below 4.5:1 (record components.button-primary-hover, used by styles.css .btn:hover).
2. '10,000+ teams' has no source: give it one or make it a labelled slot.
3. The checklist form has no action or submit handler but shows 'Thanks! Check your inbox.', a success message for a form that posts nowhere.
4. .cta uses the raw colour #FF6B6B, which is not in the record.
good.label: good

bad.text:
Method: read the page and its stylesheet.

The page looks clean and on brand. Nothing to fix.
bad.label: plausible wrong state

criteria.name: The ratio where the text sits

anchors.0: no ratio for the muted text on the card surface
anchors.2: gives about 4.39:1 for #6B7280 on #F3F4F6

anchors.0: first line is YES, NO or missing

anchors.0: no rendered check named

anchors.0: source read as settling prominence
anchors.2: says source cannot settle which element dominates, or labels its reading claimed

good.text:
UNVERIFIED

Nothing was rendered: with no browser, which element dominates the first viewport at 375px can't be measured, and source cannot settle prominence. What the source does show (claimed, not observed): the photo is 1200x900 at full width, about 257px tall at 375px wide; above the button sit a 34px headline and an 18px paragraph; the button is #15803D with white text (5.02:1). The HTML and CSS can't tell us what the eye lands on first; that needs a screenshot or measured layout at 375px. From the code, the hero photo comes first and is larger than the button, but whether the button still dominates is a rendered question.
